Onboarding showcase films (TaffyGo renders with identified source assets)
===========================================================================

Vendored asset:  ../src/main/res/raw/ — eight MP4 files, four explainers in
                 light and dark cuts. Together they are 11,993,626 bytes.
Owner:           TaffyGo for the original compositions, copy, motion, drawn UI,
                 TaffyGo marks, brand-narration text, audio placement and
                 procedural sound design. The narrator is the TaffyGo product
                 team and brand, describing Taffy in the third person; neither
                 Taffy nor the AI speaks in first person. The font, ElevenLabs
                 model and professional Helen voice remain the property of
                 their respective owners. A rendered container does not
                 transfer those rights to TaffyGo.
Licence:         TaffyGo's original work is reserved media rather than code
                 licensed under the repository LICENSE; see TRADEMARKS.md. Space Grotesk is used under the SIL Open Font License
                 1.1. No third-party logo or product artwork appears in any of
                 the eight files recorded here; see "Which films contain
                 external marks" below, which is the section that decides which
                 films may be in this directory at all.
                 The narration was generated while an active paid ElevenLabs
                 Creator subscription was observed, and the user attested that
                 the premium plan and credential were authorized for commercial
                 use. Paid-plan Outputs may be used commercially subject to the
                 ElevenLabs Terms and Prohibited Use Policy. No ownership claim
                 is made over the provider model or professional Helen voice.
Audio:           Four short English brand-narrator lines generated with
                 ElevenLabs, plus original procedural UI sound effects. There
                 is no music bed, recorded human performance or upstream audio
                 sample.
Upstream:        The containers were rendered locally from the project-authored
                 HyperFrames source described below. Narration generation and
                 normalization lineage are also recorded below.
Fetched:         NOT APPLICABLE for the MP4 containers. Narration source
                 responses were generated on 2026-08-21.
Recorded:        2026-08-23. The bytes and their 2026-08-21 record are older
                 than this date; what changed on 2026-08-23 is which files are
                 in the directory, and every measured fact below was taken
                 again from the files that remain.

Seven films were rendered; four are here
----------------------------------------

Three of the seven explainers — `compare`, `driving-licence` and `mail` —
composite official Amazon, Flipkart, Croma, Reliance Digital, Samsung,
DigiLocker, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Gmail artwork. An
official source is provenance, not permission, and no permission was recorded
from any of those eight owners. OD-094 in `docs/open-decisions.md` is the
launch blocker that owns the decision owner by owner, and those three films,
their six final posters and their strings are not in the tree.

The rights position is per stem rather than per set, and the four here clear
it: their only non-TaffyGo visual material is Space Grotesk, rasterised into
the frames under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and `page-tools` additionally
shows this repository's own synthetic diagram fixture. That is why they may
ship while the other three may not.

The three held stems, their posters and this record's fuller form remain
recoverable from Git at `cff4504c^`. Re-rendering them without the marks is
not available: the authoring project the earlier record named as the remedy
was ignored by Git and is not on this host, which was checked on 2026-08-23
rather than assumed.

Checksums and byte counts of the shipped MP4s
----------------------------------------------

The `sha256_` and `bytes_` facts are checked against every file in `res/raw`
in both directions by `tools/lib/vendored_assets.py`. Adding, removing or
changing a film without changing this record fails the files lane. That
bidirectional check is also what keeps a held stem out: a line here with no
file is a finding in its own right, so this record cannot carry the three that
left.

sha256_taffy_showcase_form_dark_mp4=7087d555569457d5b03fbcd1502a985305a99de358eac34450c32c3c3e3e09ca
bytes_taffy_showcase_form_dark_mp4=1293037
sha256_taffy_showcase_form_light_mp4=a661b2bbcdb23fdb1c648fab473d969e48a2e4c3cf161ea755ed420553a75ffc

Every one of these sixteen facts is the value the 2026-08-21 record carried,
re-verified against the file on disk on 2026-08-23. The bytes are the reviewed
bytes; nothing was re-encoded to make this record shorter.

Render and package identity
---------------------------

The source was the project-authored standalone project at
`videos-harness/taffygo-feature-intro/`. That directory was ignored by Git, so
it was never part of a repository checkout, and it is no longer on this host —
its seven HTML compositions, local asset manifest, batch files, proof,
generation and normalization attestations, and the two audio-source scripts
were the render record. The package scripts pinned HyperFrames 0.8.6 exactly.

The approved visual streams were frozen before the corrected brand narration
was generated. Every corrected-narration light/dark batch then used the
high-quality 30 fps render with strict lint, runtime, layout, motion, contrast
and variable checking:

  npm run render -- -c <composition> --batch batch/themes.json \
    --output "renders/taffy_showcase_<stem>_{theme}_master.mp4" \
    --batch-concurrency 1 --batch-fail-fast --quality high --fps 30 \
    --strict-all --no-best-effort --strict-variables

No explicit `--skill` flag was passed to either the frozen-visual render
commands or the corrected-narration raw render commands. Project metadata is an
authoring label, not evidence that an invocation flag was supplied.

Fresh browser capture made the raw corrected-narration visual streams
near-identical to the approved visuals, but their encoded video packets were
not byte-for-byte identical. The raw HyperFrames renders were therefore used
only as the source of their new AAC streams. The final stable masters were made
with one copy-only mux: video from the frozen prior master, audio from the raw
corrected-narration render, and no audio or video re-encoding:

  ffmpeg -i <frozen-prior-master> \
    -i <raw-corrected-narration-render> \
    -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c copy -movflags +faststart <stable-master>

This preserved the exact approved visual packet stream while carrying the exact
AAC packets HyperFrames rendered from the corrected narration and unchanged
procedural effects. The stable masters under `renders/` were then copied as the
Android resources without another mux:

  cp <stable-master> <android.mp4>

Because the source project is gone, that pipeline is history rather than a
procedure anyone can run again. It is kept here because it says what these
bytes are, which is the question a provenance record exists to answer.

Measured on 2026-08-23 from the eight files in this directory
--------------------------------------------------------------

  Video        H.264 High, 1080 x 1350, yuv420p, 30/1 fps.
  Audio        AAC-LC, 48 kHz, stereo. English brand narration plus sparse
               UI effects; no music.
  Durations    9.2 seconds for form and weekly-review; 9.4 seconds for job;
               9.5 seconds for page-tools. Light and dark cuts have equal
               duration.
  Fast start   `moov` begins at byte 36 before `mdat` in all eight files.
               `mdat` begins at byte 9,385 for the 9.2-second films, 9,553 for
               job, and 9,645 for page-tools. These positions were read from
               each container, not inferred from duration.
  Loudness     Integrated loudness ranges from -17.10 to -16.56 LUFS; true
               peak ranges from -3.00 to -2.95 dBTP.

  Per film     form -17.06 LUFS / -3.00 dBTP;
               weekly-review -17.10 LUFS / -2.99 dBTP;
               job -16.77 LUFS / -2.97 dBTP;
               page-tools -16.56 LUFS / -2.95 dBTP.

The tool was `ffmpeg -af loudnorm=print_format=json` on FFmpeg build
`N-126175-g0056dd32fd-20260816`, reading `input_i` and `input_tp`. Seven of the
eight values are identical to the 2026-08-21 record. Page-tools measures -16.56
where that record says -16.60, and its file is byte-identical to the file that
record describes — so the difference is the decoder, not the film. A loudness
figure is a measurement of a decoded signal and therefore of the decoder as
well; a checksum is not, which is why the checksums above are the facts the
gate checks and this section is prose.

Stream hashes, and why one kind of them travels and the other does not
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

The following are identical in the light and dark cut of each film, measured on
2026-08-23. The first is the copied AAC packet stream
(`ffmpeg -map 0:a:0 -c copy -f md5`); the second is the decoded PCM
(`ffmpeg -map 0:a:0 -f md5`, which selects `pcm_s16le`):

  form             AAC c8afc4dbff60ed1cadbf4d2dcd34d3ef
                   PCM 67b56725e7816682dd0ba6d957c487cf
  weekly-review    AAC 3680c6ca0b19e42ff9a5ca52b0444113
                   PCM 00535c19d3791c30784d4081536da48c
  job              AAC c00c5fc073b069abdc3b034c94d7466e
                   PCM 50b0041010ade6684426b2d3f548be11
  page-tools       AAC cd9f5ebc9b1bb60ae76e45fa4e6fea8c
                   PCM 63e1a0d16595b93a1746fa1fa06325fe

All four AAC packet hashes equal the values the 2026-08-21 record carried, so
the audio packets in these files are provably the reviewed packets. None of the
four PCM hashes equals that record's value, which was produced by FFmpeg 8.1.2.
The decoded length is exact in both builds — form decodes to 1,766,400 bytes of
stereo `s16le`, which is 9.2 seconds at 48 kHz to the sample — so this is two
AAC decoders differing in their output samples, not a truncated or altered
file. The packet hash is a property of the file; the PCM hash is a property of
the file and the decoder together, and it is recorded with its build named so
that a future reader can tell those two cases apart instead of reading a
mismatch as damage.

Original procedural audio sources embedded in the films
--------------------------------------------------------

All three frozen sources are 48 kHz stereo PCM WAVs generated deterministically
by FFmpeg's `lavfi` sources. They total 221,034 bytes, are not Android
resources of their own, and ship only after AAC encoding inside the MP4s. Their
exact generation commands and placement envelopes were in
`videos-harness/taffygo-feature-intro/scripts/generate-sfx.sh` and the seven
compositions, neither of which is on this host any more.

All three are named here rather than pruned to a subset. The source project
recorded the effects against the set of seven compositions and did not state
which effect appears in which film, so naming only some of them would be a
claim this record cannot support.

  taffy-soft-invoke.wav
      80,718 bytes; 0.42 seconds.
      Source:
        aevalsrc=0.24*sin(2*PI*(340*t+280*t*t))+
        0.11*sin(2*PI*(680*t+410*t*t)):s=48000:d=0.42
      Filters, in order:
        afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.028
        afade=t=out:st=0.17:d=0.25
        highpass=f=180, lowpass=f=5000, volume=0.65
        pan=stereo|c0=0.95*c0|c1=0.85*c0
      Output: 48 kHz, two-channel, pcm_s16le.
      SHA-256 834809e68b9449c0c6e7cd595bc347346d6b5ed68715a9c7c3ff9d6b6e635a7e

  taffy-approval-tap.wav
      34,638 bytes; 0.18 seconds.
      Source:
        aevalsrc=(1-exp(-220*t))*exp(-24*t)*
        (0.45*sin(2*PI*620*t)+0.20*sin(2*PI*980*t)):s=48000:d=0.18
      Filters, in order:
        afade=t=out:st=0.06:d=0.12
        highpass=f=220, lowpass=f=3300, volume=0.44
        pan=stereo|c0=0.84*c0|c1=0.96*c0
      Output: 48 kHz, two-channel, pcm_s16le.
      SHA-256 1e05b973af78fc6228825986383d6dc1cdb6766b7c89bb554699bd51739a534d

  taffy-result-settle.wav
      105,678 bytes; 0.55 seconds.
      Sources:
        sine=frequency=523.25:duration=0.38:sample_rate=48000
        sine=frequency=659.25:duration=0.32:sample_rate=48000
        sine=frequency=880:duration=0.25:sample_rate=48000
      First source filters:
        afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025, afade=t=out:st=0.10:d=0.28
        volume=0.22
        pan=stereo|c0=0.96*c0|c1=0.78*c0
      Second source filters:
        afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.025, afade=t=out:st=0.08:d=0.24
        adelay=120|120
        volume=0.18, pan=stereo|c0=0.78*c0|c1=0.96*c0
      Third source filters:
        afade=t=in:st=0:d=0.020, afade=t=out:st=0.06:d=0.19
        adelay=230|230
        volume=0.07, pan=stereo|c0=0.88*c0|c1=0.88*c0
      Mix filters:
        amix=inputs=3:duration=longest:normalize=0
        lowpass=f=4300, aecho=0.8:0.5:40|90:0.08|0.03
        apad=pad_dur=0.55, atrim=0:0.55, volume=10.8
      Output: 48 kHz, two-channel, pcm_s16le.
      SHA-256 3339708367934e5ed6b2af06dcf7ae1cb2a49133aa3ce8cebca0945b319240f5

Provider-generated brand narration embedded in the films
---------------------------------------------------------

Seven English brand-narrator lines were generated through ElevenLabs between
local file-write times 2026-08-21T17:19:46Z and 2026-08-21T17:19:54Z; four of
them are embedded in the films here, and those four are the ones recorded
below. Those timestamps are local filesystem evidence, not provider response
timestamps. The narrator is the TaffyGo product team and brand, speaking about
Taffy in the third person; neither Taffy nor the AI speaks in first person. The
API generation used the script defaults with no voice or model override:

  Provider       ElevenLabs text to speech.
  Model          eleven_multilingual_v2.
  Voice          XB0fDUnXU5powFXDhCwa. A redacted, same-session read-only
                 `/v1/voices/` lookup on 2026-08-21 resolved the exact ID to
                 Helen, category `professional`.
  Output         mp3_44100_128; measured as 44.1 kHz, 128 kbps, mono MP3.
  Settings       stability 0.62; similarity boost 0.72; style 0.12;
                 speaker boost enabled.
  Omitted        speed, language code, text normalization, seed, previous text
                 and next text were not sent, so no values are asserted.
  Missing        request IDs, provider character counts and provider generation
                 timestamps were not captured and cannot be inferred from the
                 audio files.
  Determinism    not guaranteed. No seed was sent; SHA-256 freezes the exact
                 returned bytes instead of claiming byte-for-byte recreation.
  Credential     read only from the generation process environment. No key,
                 key fingerprint, authorization header or account identity is
                 stored in this record.

The four raw responses whose audio is in this directory total 395,982 bytes:

  02-form.mp3
      91,577 bytes; 5.665669 seconds.
      SHA-256 8d7657d60b2ef45bd195263fcdce7fa1af0d486e3ed8a2e1cd48afab587a11b3
      Script: Taffy fills boring details with permission, asks what you know,
              and waits to submit.
  04-weekly-review.mp3
      84,471 bytes; 5.201270 seconds.
      SHA-256 a4d2e8daad2e9aebe684b9479b6313543f295c3b769cb2e624e45980f908e7c6
      Script: Taffy blocks ads and trackers, shows time spent, and suggests a
              healthier limit.
  05-job.mp3
      100,772 bytes; 6.222948 seconds.
      SHA-256 c7b839bccd5258632343e326f525378566fb24e47e4efdeabda5240fe04fa8f6
      Script: Taffy reads tabs, cites facts, builds an infographic, and offers
              twelve export formats.
  07-page-tools.mp3
      119,162 bytes; 7.383946 seconds.
      SHA-256 90b29bc2f19530bb797e7bb7d49fe76122d6ada439eb6d8c861829084c930570
      Script: Taffy finds images and videos, asks before downloading, then
              summarises and translates. We nearly forgot those.

`scripts/normalize-voiceover.mjs` used FFmpeg 8.1.2 for measured two-pass
loudness normalization, then resampled to 48 kHz and wrote one-channel signed
16-bit PCM WAV. Targets were -19 LUFS integrated loudness, 7 LU loudness range
and -3 dBTP true peak. The four normalized sources behind these films total
2,349,802 bytes:

  02-form.wav
      543,982 bytes; 5.665667 seconds.
      SHA-256 7288af31051e0448a9236aaeef442b0f1d30c2381f07dc4c48646a070a6f6e07
  04-weekly-review.wav
      499,400 bytes; 5.201271 seconds.
      SHA-256 db5999df0e246f626195be0ec5d0a44795e4200c6953bc6731c09dda2e81b66e
  05-job.wav
      597,482 bytes; 6.222958 seconds.
      SHA-256 8ebcd24d1772d62975b89c67652cdd040bfb9e7591e3ec24e2863c42509e2926
  07-page-tools.wav
      708,938 bytes; 7.383958 seconds.
      SHA-256 946213d95e23402b875dc5d160aa8fede51fad3cec1b588b233732c59a70938e

Each composition referenced its normalized WAV directly. Narration was placed
at unity gain with a 0.04-second fade-in and 0.08-second fade-out:

  form             track 91; 0.550 to 6.215667 seconds.
  weekly-review    track 93; 0.550 to 5.751271 seconds.
  job              track 94; 0.550 to 6.772958 seconds.
  page-tools       track 96; 0.550 to 7.933958 seconds.

The renderer mixed the mono WAV and procedural stereo effects into the 48 kHz
stereo AAC stream inside each MP4. The raw MP3 and normalized WAV sources are
not Android resources, and they are not on this host any more; their byte
counts and hashes are kept so that a recovered copy can be identified as the
one these films were made from.

A redacted, read-only subscription lookup in the same working session after
generation reported tier `creator`, status `active`, without retrieving account
identity. That observation does not establish the exact provider response time
for any individual generated file. The user also attested that the premium plan
and credential were authorized for commercial usage and directed this use to
proceed. The ElevenLabs Terms, last updated 2026-03-31, and billing
documentation state that paid-plan Outputs may be used commercially, subject to
the Terms and Prohibited Use Policy:

  https://elevenlabs.io/terms-of-use
  https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/billing

TaffyGo authored the narration text. This record makes no ownership claim over
the ElevenLabs model or professional Helen voice and does not waive any
provider condition.

Frozen visual sources and rights
--------------------------------

The following exact frozen files are visible in the rendered frames of the four
films here. The SHA-256 values identify those source bytes.

  TaffyGo marks
      Repository-owned `brand/png/taffygo-mark-color-on-{light,dark}.png`.
      Frozen source SHA-256 values:
      light caa965b2325d7d0d7dc3dee2a2eb4b5ecc3f0f9f0858df6f7d9729eccf605ee8
      dark  61fab10b771aa9bcd4a8b612ece85f42b95f179051878f911b79ef42a39c0d96

  Space Grotesk 2.000
      Frozen WOFF2 SHA-256
      2a58e2d03e6377126327a2769b177ed250327e6aace74e02fbf64e4637084d94.
      Source: https://github.com/floriankarsten/space-grotesk
      Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1; the source project carried OFL.txt.

  Page-tools diagram
      Repository-owned synthetic fixture copied byte-for-byte from
      `test-fixtures/web/origins/primary/media/diagram.svg`.
      SHA-256 3ffd07cdb9230e8754729909c375e634505782959402cc27a624d80380f768d1.

That is the complete list. The eight third-party and government assets the
earlier record named belong to the three films that are not here, and their
official sources left with them; `cff4504c^` holds that section unchanged for
anyone taking the OD-094 decision forward.

The local GSAP 3.14.2 runtime and HyperFrames 0.8.6 CLI were render tools, not
visual or audio source assets copied into the MP4 containers. Their own terms
still govern running those tools; this record does not relabel them as TaffyGo
source merely because their output contains TaffyGo-authored motion.

The multilingual greeting in page-tools relies on the capture browser's
fallback fonts for scripts Space Grotesk does not contain; the exact fallback
font family was not declared in the composition and is therefore not asserted
here.

Which films contain external marks
-----------------------------------

  form, weekly-review, job and page-tools, light and dark
      No third-party logo or product artwork. These still use Space Grotesk;
      page-tools also uses the repository-owned diagram fixture.

  compare, driving-licence and mail
      Not in this directory. Each carried official third-party or Government of
      India artwork with no recorded permission, which is OD-094.

Reach, use and removal trigger
------------------------------

`ShowcaseVideo.kt` names all eight through `R.raw`, and `ShowcaseVideoView`
plays the selected file. The onboarding module's resources reach the Chromium
APK resource graph through `taffy-core/app/android/tools/resource_mounts.py`
and the generated `kotlin_sources.gni` list.

A film returns to this directory only with a record of permission from every
owner whose mark it carries, added here as its own named section. A film leaves
if that permission is withdrawn or if the composition changes; either way its
`sha256_` and `bytes_` lines move with it, in the same change, because the
files lane checks this record in both directions. The record leaves with the
directory if the showcase films leave the product.
